open_points.subject: A04 customer erasure and the revision/last-changed pair
open_points.text: An erasure is not one of them: it keeps no revision (rule 1).
open_points.question: Must Customer erasure move its last-changed instant, as State 1 says, or is it excluded as A04 Required test 11 now says? State 1 also says revision and last-changed move exactly together, while erasure keeps neither revision nor the recorded instant.
options: Erasure does not move last-changed; it removes the revision/last-changed pair and writes only the erased-mark and audit instants.
Erasure moves last-changed and revision before both are removed atomically.
Erasure preserves a final revision/last-changed pair after erasure.
open_points.default_guess: Erasure does not move last-changed; it removes the pair and records the erasure through the erased-mark and audit instants.

open_points.subject: A04 revision-changing operation clock readings
open_points.text: moves the record's revision by exactly one and sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: How many UTC wall-clock readings does one accepted action take for its last-changed instant, lifecycle-mark instant, audit-entry instant and, when applicable, the default relationship-end date?
options: Take one wall-clock reading for the operation and derive every instant and today's date written by that operation from it.
Take one reading for each field or record written.
Take separate readings for the domain record and audit entry, but share readings within each.
open_points.default_guess: Take one wall-clock reading after admission for the whole atomic action and use it for every instant it writes.

witness.initial: A Customer has revision 4 and no ended mark; the UTC wall clock is about to cross midnight.
events: The owner ends the relationship without supplying a date.
Registry writes the ended mark, the Customer's last-changed instant and the audit entry while the clock crosses midnight.
outcomes: One shared reading gives the end date, mark, last-changed instant and audit instant one consistent operation time.
Separate readings can give the default end date from one day and the record or audit instants from the next day.
witness.observer: The owner comparing the Customer card with the audit log and retention date

open_points.subject: A04 sampling point for the current instant
open_points.text: sets its last-changed instant to the current instant
open_points.question: At what event in an atomic action is the current instant sampled: request admission, acquisition of the store's write lock, immediately before applying the change, or commit?
options: Sample after the action has acquired the write lock and passed its checks, immediately before applying the atomic change.
Sample when the request is admitted, before it may wait for the write lock.
Sample at commit after the changes have been prepared.
open_points.default_guess: Sample once under the write lock immediately before applying the accepted change.

witness.initial: Two accepted Customer changes contend for the store's write lock.
events: Caller A arrives first and waits before acquiring the lock.
Caller B later reaches its action, and the transactions acquire the lock in an order different from request arrival.
outcomes: Admission-time sampling can make stored last-changed and audit instants run opposite to the committed revision order.
Under-lock sampling makes the instants follow the order in which revisions are committed.
witness.observer: The owner reading successive revisions and their audit entries
